chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Plan for an abandoned firehouse as a traditional music hall
summary: Danny wants an old firehouse in his birthplace neighborhood as a small opera house and museum where youngsters can hear traditional music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: There's an old abandoned firehouse I've been trying to get, right in the middle of the Black neighborhood that I was born and raised in, and I want to use that as a little opera house, something like that Nashville thing that they have for opera [sic: Grand Old Opry], have a little place where young Blacks or any Black can come in and hear traditional music, and keep the tradition. It means that the music of Armstrong and Oliver and Noone and Bunk Johnson and Buddy Bolden; you come there and you can hear this music. A little museum. A little place where you can come there and hear youngsters playing it. Because youngsters are still interested in the music. When they're hear it in the parades, on the street marching along... There's still second-line, and you have a joyous time, give a joyous noise unto the Lord. But when they get out there now, they're
giving a joyous noice to the Devil, because he's cutting up in a rambunctious manner.

So that's a place... I would like to get this hall. Because I have a little competition with some young men in New Orleans; so after I told them about it, now they're interested in it, too. But they're more aggressive than I am. I think they have a better chance of getting it. But I still could use it if they get it, because they look to me when they get on the books as something... They always say that Danny Barker showed them how to do this. I'm interested in youth.
